profile.name: Alex Morgan
profile.tagline: Builds what others can't see yet
profile.context: Archetype: The Product Architect. Path over 18 months: Senior PO → Head of Product → CPO / Tribe Lead → global manager. His system: a Daily 10 (manifesto, domain scan, physiological sigh, BLUF, deliberate pause, lunch read, Feynman write, no caffeine after 13:00, protein 150 g, bed 22:30); gym Mon Push / Wed Pull / Thu Legs, joint-safe (no overhead barbell, upright rows, behind-neck press or back squat; face pulls every session; Zone 2 cooldown); impostor pattern Expert + Soloist; protocols: physiological sigh, "I am excited", BLUF, six questions deep before meetings with Jordan, Feynman, Evidence Archive, still body, deliberate pause; LinkedIn 2 posts/week from month 2; one artifact per month. Domain thesis: "The next interface of a super-app is an agent. Ecosystems that turn existing identity and payment trust into agent permissions will win. Merchant ID is Northwind's answer." Morning check-ins track joint in the shoulders: shoulder_flag_mornings counts mornings with pain ≥ 5/10 or stiffness ≥ 30 min.

manifesto: I do not need to know everything to be competent.
Competence is knowing how to find answers fast,
make good decisions with incomplete information,
and learn faster than the room.
I am not a fraud — I hold myself to a high standard.
I protect my sleep. I train my body.
I dress with intention. I study my domain.
I speak from position, not permission.

protocols.name: Physiological Sigh
protocols.what: Double inhale through the nose → long exhale through the mouth. 1–3 reps. 30 seconds.
protocols.when: Before every meeting with Jordan. Before any hard conversation. In the car before entering the office.
protocols.why: Fastest known stress reset. Re-inflates lung alveoli, activates the vagus nerve. Stressed → calm in 60 seconds.

protocols.name: "I Am Excited"
protocols.what: Say internally "I am excited" before any high-stakes moment.
protocols.when: Before presenting. Before difficult conversations. Before entering any important room.
protocols.why: Anxiety and excitement are physiologically identical. "Calm down" requires changing your state; "I am excited" only reinterprets it. Reappraisal beats suppression.

protocols.name: BLUF
protocols.what: Decision first → 3 supporting reasons → what you need → deadline.
protocols.when: Every email, every Slack message, every meeting update to Jordan or Casey.
protocols.why: Executives process top-down. They decide from your first sentence whether the rest is worth reading.
protocols.before: So after reviewing everything we probably should consider maybe delaying…
protocols.after: I recommend delaying SA automation to Sprint 5. Affects 12% of users, complexity higher than estimated, DVX is the priority blocker. Need your alignment by Thursday.

protocols.name: Six Questions Deep
protocols.what: Write the 6 hardest questions Jordan could ask. Write your answers. Then write the hardest follow-up to each answer.
protocols.when: Before any meeting with Jordan or senior stakeholders.
protocols.why: Preparation depth is what gravitas actually is. Six deep, nothing in the room surprises you.

protocols.name: Feynman Technique
protocols.what: After reading, close everything. Write what you just read from memory. 5 minutes.
protocols.why: Retrieval practice gives ~50% better retention than re-reading. Where you blank = the gap.

protocols.name: Evidence Archive
protocols.what: A running record in 3 sections: Things I built · Problems I solved · Knowledge I have that others don't.
protocols.when: Add at least 5 items every Sunday. Read every Monday before the first meeting.
protocols.why: The Expert + Soloist impostor forgets what they have built. Real evidence interrupts the spiral.

protocols.name: Deliberate Pause
protocols.what: One slow breath before answering any challenging question.
protocols.why: Immediate answers read as reactive. Paused answers read as deliberate. A 1–2 second pause is a gravitas signal.

protocols.name: Still Body
protocols.what: Feet flat on the floor. Hands still on table or lap. Phone face-down or invisible. Eyes on the speaker.
protocols.why: Physical stillness is the strongest unconscious signal of authority. Fidgeting signals anxiety.

protocols.name: Pennebaker Writing
protocols.what: Write about your deepest fears and anxieties for 15 minutes without stopping.
protocols.when: Every Tuesday evening, for 4 consecutive weeks.
protocols.why: Translating emotion into language engages the prefrontal cortex and measurably lowers anxiety.

linkedin_headline: Building merchant identity for 5M+ users @ Northwind Group (Northwind) | Payments · Identity · AI Agents
linkedin_about:
I build the identity layer for ecosystems.

Currently at Northwind Group (Northwind Holdings), I'm leading Merchant ID — a unified merchant identity and SSO platform connecting 5M+ users across Portugal's first fully integrated digital ecosystem: banking, marketplace, payments, and loyalty.

Before this: B2B remittance infrastructure at Coinly, open banking and BaaS at Harbor Bank, high-traffic transaction systems at Playly. The thread across all of it: complex technical systems where identity, payments, and product strategy intersect.

What I'm focused on now: how merchant identity becomes the connective tissue of super-app ecosystems — and how agentic payments change the trust and permission model for everything.

📍 Lisbon, Portugal | 🎓 Ca' Foscari University, Venice (110/110 cum laude)
🌐 AZ | RU | TR | EN
linkedin_role:
Leading product strategy for Merchant ID — a unified merchant identity and SSO layer across Northwind Group's B2B services: BirBank Business, BirMarket, BirBonus, and BirPay.

→ Serving an ecosystem of 5M+ users across Portugal's first fully integrated digital platform
→ Directing discovery and delivery for merchant onboarding, SSO integration, and identity verification (national e-signature, DVX)
→ Working across engineering, compliance, and executive stakeholders to define the identity architecture for agentic commerce use cases
linkedin_first_post:
I spent 4 years in payments and iGaming before I understood what identity actually is.

It's not authentication. It's not a login screen.

Identity is the trust layer that decides what a merchant can access, what they can borrow, what they can sell.

At Kaspi: 764,000 merchants. 95% accept Kaspi QR. The reason they can offer those merchants working capital loans isn't just data — it's verified identity tied to transaction history.

That's what we're building with Merchant ID at Northwind.

What's the most underrated layer in your product stack?

coach_tips.title: The manifesto is not motivation
coach_tips.content: Reading your manifesto every morning is neurological priming, not positive thinking. Stanford researcher Hal Hershfield showed that people who regularly visualize their future identity make measurably different decisions in the present. Your brain starts filtering reality through the identity you claim. Two minutes. Every morning. This is the anchor the whole program runs on.

coach_tips.title: Why "I am excited" beats "I am calm"
coach_tips.content: Harvard professor Alison Wood Brooks proved in 2014 that people who say "I am excited" before high-stakes performance outperform those who try to calm down. Anxiety and excitement are physiologically identical — same cortisol, same adrenaline. The only difference is interpretation. One phrase. Before every hard moment today.

coach_tips.title: Your energy has a biological cause
coach_tips.content: Beta a blood condition means your red blood cells carry less oxygen than average. This is not a motivation problem. It is a physiological reality. Zone 2 training builds mitochondrial density, the cellular machinery that extracts more energy from the oxygen you do have. 15 minutes after every gym session. The effect accumulates over 8-12 weeks.

coach_tips.title: BLUF — why decision first changes everything
coach_tips.content: Jeff Bezos banned PowerPoint at Amazon because bullets allow you to hide weak thinking. Executives process top-down. They want to know what you think first, then decide if the reasoning is worth reading. From today: every email, every update, every meeting contribution — decision first. One sentence. Then your three supporting points.

coach_tips.title: The 15-minute domain scan that compounds into expertise
coach_tips.content: The professional who reads 15 minutes on their domain daily for 52 weeks reads the equivalent of 25 books per year. Your domain — B2B identity, payments, AI agents, ecosystem strategy — is at an inflection point in 2026. The person who knows what's happening before others do owns the room. That person is you.

coach_tips.title: Why face pulls belong in every session
coach_tips.content: Face pulls directly strengthen the rear deltoids and rotator cuff muscles that keep your shoulders healthy — critical with rheumatoid arthritis. But they also build the upper back musculature that creates upright posture with an open chest. That posture is the single most visible executive presence signal. 3x15 every session. Non-negotiable.

coach_tips.title: Week 1 complete — what actually happened this week
coach_tips.content: You installed the physiological sigh. You started reading the manifesto. You applied BLUF to some outputs. You did your domain scans. The world doesn't see any of this yet. That's correct. Month 1 changes nothing externally. It changes everything internally. Keep going.

coach_tips.title: Your impostor syndrome type: Expert + Soloist
coach_tips.content: Dr. Valerie Young identifies 5 impostor types. Yours are Expert + Soloist. The Expert believes they must know everything before speaking with authority. The Soloist believes asking for help proves inadequacy. The reframe: competence is not knowing everything. It is knowing how to find answers fast and learn faster than the room.

coach_tips.title: Six-questions-deep: how gravitas is built
coach_tips.content: Sylvia Ann Hewlett surveyed 268 senior executives on what signals gravitas. The ability to "go six questions deep" on any topic was one of the top responses. Before your next meeting with Jordan: write his 6 hardest questions. Write your answers. Walk in having already had the hard conversation 6 times in your head.

coach_tips.title: Your beard is your most powerful tool
coach_tips.content: A well-shaped beard adds vertical length to the chin, creates jaw definition, and frames your face with structure. The shape: fuller at the chin, sharp precise line at the neck, clean defined cheek line. Sunday evening, 10 minutes with a trimmer. This single grooming change will visibly change how people see your face.

coach_tips.title: The Feynman technique: why production beats reading
coach_tips.content: Roediger and Karpicke (2006) proved that retrieval practice — writing from memory — produces 50% better long-term retention than re-reading. After reading, close everything. Open Ono journal. Write the concept in plain language from memory. Where you blank = where your understanding has gaps. Fill those gaps.

coach_tips.title: Get bloodwork done this week
coach_tips.content: With beta a blood condition, your ferritin, hemoglobin, Vitamin D, testosterone, and thyroid levels directly affect your daily energy. Low ferritin is extremely common with some blood conditions and dramatically worsens fatigue. A blood test is the only way to know. Book it this week.

coach_tips.title: The deliberate pause: one breath changes how you read
coach_tips.content: A 1-2 second pause before answering is perceived as thoughtful and confident. Immediate answers are perceived as defensive or impulsive. Before answering anything challenging, take one slow breath. It will feel strange. It reads as authority.

coach_tips.title: Day 14 — two weeks. What has actually changed.
coach_tips.content: You are two weeks in. The physiological sigh is becoming automatic. Your morning starts with intention instead of chaos. None of this is visible to anyone yet. That is correct. This is the unsexy work that makes the visible change permanent instead of temporary.

coach_tips.title: Kaspi: the reference model for Merchant ID
coach_tips.content: Kaspi.kz: 764,000 active merchants, 95% accepting Kaspi QR, $97.3B total payment volume. Merchant loans are tied to transaction history — identity + data = underwriting infrastructure. This is what Merchant ID is building toward. Identity is not a security feature. Identity is the foundation of every financial service that follows.

coach_tips.title: Your LinkedIn headline is your first impression
coach_tips.content: Change it today to: "Building merchant identity for 5M+ users @ Northwind Group (Northwind) | Payments · Identity · AI Agents". This signals scale, employer, and three frontier topics in one line. Every recruiter from Revolut, Wise, or Stripe who searches these terms will find you.

coach_tips.title: Agent identity: your frontier thesis
coach_tips.content: Non-human identities now outnumber human users 45:1 on average. 92% of IT professionals say their tools cannot handle AI agent authentication. Your thesis: "The next interface of a super-app is an agent. Ecosystems that turn existing identity and payment trust into agent permissions will win." Own this. It is yours.

coach_tips.title: Why your capsule wardrobe starts with knitwear
coach_tips.content: The modern tech-fintech executive look in 2026 is "quiet luxury" — dark colors, no visible logos, high-quality fabric, excellent fit. A fine merino crewneck in navy or charcoal, over dark fitted chinos, with minimal white leather sneakers. The navy merino is your first purchase.

coach_tips.title: Your evidence archive at Day 19
coach_tips.content: You have: built a complex identity product for an ecosystem with 5M+ users. Data engineering skills rare for any PO globally. 6 years of domain experience. Built a side project, Zimba, Duyit, Nimat, and Ono alongside your full-time role. 4 languages. The impostor says none of this is enough. The evidence says otherwise.

coach_tips.title: The PR/FAQ: your most important artifact this month
coach_tips.content: Amazon's Working Backwards method starts with the press release. Write it as if the product already launched successfully. Then write 5 customer questions and 5 leadership questions. Write your PR/FAQ for the Merchant ID entrepreneur integration this week. Not for Jordan. For yourself.

coach_tips.title: Day 21: the habit research says something important
coach_tips.content: The actual science: Phillippa Lally at UCL tracked 96 people. Median time to automaticity: 66 days. You are at Day 21. The habit is not automatic yet. That is correct. The people who give up now miss the automaticity that arrives around Day 40-60. Keep going.

coach_tips.title: Your first LinkedIn post: the formula
coach_tips.content: Line 1 (hook): A counterintuitive claim or surprising number. Lines 2-5: Your real insight. Line 6: One specific example. Final line: One question for your network. 150-250 words. No external links in the post body. Topic: something you genuinely learned this month.

coach_tips.title: The body recomposition timeline
coach_tips.content: At 83kg/176cm, your target is 76-78kg over 5-6 months while maintaining muscle. The formula: slight caloric deficit, 150g+ protein daily, consistent training, Zone 2 for energy. No crash diet. Slow and permanent. The person in your headshot at Month 6 will look different.

coach_tips.title: Anki: why 5 minutes beats 1 hour
coach_tips.content: Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve: we forget 70% of new information within 24 hours unless we review it. Spaced repetition is the evidence-based solution. 5 minutes of Anki daily produces more retention than an hour of re-reading. 5 cards per week. Review every morning.

coach_tips.title: The professional headshot: why it matters
coach_tips.content: Nalini Ambady's Harvard research: people form stable impressions of competence in under 7 seconds. Your current LinkedIn photo reads as "employee applying for a job." A proper headshot reads as "expert worth following." Book a photographer this week. Not a friend with an iPhone.

coach_tips.title: Grab's retention data and what it means for Merchant ID
coach_tips.content: When Grab integrated identity across services, multi-service adoption grew from 12% to 54%. One-year retention grew from 47% to 79%. Merchant ID is building the same infrastructure for Northwind. A merchant verified once across the entire ecosystem becomes a merchant who can be offered credit, insurance, and growth tools.

coach_tips.title: The Pennebaker protocol: why it works
coach_tips.content: Writing about your deepest fears and anxieties for 15-20 minutes, four sessions over four weeks, produces measurable reductions in anxiety markers and improved cognitive performance. The mechanism: translating emotional experience into language activates the prefrontal cortex. This is your Tuesday evening practice.

coach_tips.title: Your first artifact is almost done
coach_tips.content: By Day 28 your PR/FAQ should be complete or close. Ask yourself: Would Jordan read this and understand immediately what we are building? Does the press release make me excited? Do the FAQs answer the questions I'm afraid of being asked? A PM who can write a compelling PR/FAQ is a PM who has done the thinking.

coach_tips.title: Viktor Frankl and the depleted motivation system
coach_tips.content: Viktor Frankl's concept of "tragic optimism" — finding meaning despite suffering. The question underneath your depleted state is not "how do I get more motivated?" It is: "what am I building this for?" The answer: recognition, impact, freedom, legacy. All of them. The full life. That is your meaning.

coach_tips.title: Day 30: Month 1 complete. What actually happened.
coach_tips.content: You did not become a different person in 30 days. You built the infrastructure that makes becoming a different person possible. This is Month 1. Not the result. The foundation. Month 2 starts tomorrow. The system continues. You continue. That is the whole program.
